JPMorgan Chase has invested more than $5 billion in companies supporting U.S. national security and industrial capacity, committing roughly half its planned decade-long investment budget in the program's first year. The pace could prompt the country's largest bank to expand its original $10 billion commitment, co-President Doug Petno told CNBC. The investments form part of JPMorgan's Security and Resiliency Initiative, launched last October amid concerns about America's dependence on foreign manufacturing and critical supplies. Although defense companies are prominent recipients, the money also supports manufacturing, frontier technologies, and other industries considered essential to economic security. These direct investments fall under a broader $1.5 trillion financing initiative announced in 2025. Most of the bank's investments remain undisclosed, but two known recipients, Hadrian and Castelion, show how JPMorgan is targeting both weapons development and the factories needed to expand production. JPMorgan in August helped lead a $1.4 billion funding round for Hadrian, which develops automated factories producing components for defense, aerospace, and maritime customers. Its operations use robotics to increase domestic manufacturing capacity. That same month, the bank participated in Castelion's approximately $1 billion financing round. Founded by former SpaceX engineers, Castelion is developing Blackbeard, a hypersonic missile the company describes as designed for lower costs and mass production. Its funding announcement identified JPMorgan's Strategic Investment Group as a co-leader of the equity financing. The amounts raised by those companies represent their overall funding rounds, rather than JPMorgan's individual contributions. The bank has not publicly detailed the size of every stake. Todd Combs, the former Berkshire Hathaway executive leading JPMorgan's investment group, said the strategy emphasizes businesses the bank can support over an extended period. "Our approach is to find generational companies and partner with them for the long term," Combs said in a statement. Petno said the bank is finding businesses that have developed ways to manufacture important products domestically, reducing dependence on overseas suppliers. He also credited Combs with moving quickly since taking charge of the group. The initiative reflects concerns championed by CEO Jamie Dimon about vulnerabilities exposed by wars, trade disputes and concentrated supply chains. Fighting in Ukraine and the Middle East, alongside tensions with China, has increased attention on access to energy, industrial components and military equipment. For JPMorgan, taking ownership stakes also changes its financial exposure. Lending to companies and advising on transactions are familiar banking businesses. Investing directly in younger enterprises ties returns more closely to whether their technologies succeed and their operations can grow. The bank previously stepped back from private equity investing, spinning out One Equity Partners more than a decade ago, according to the outlet. Alongside those investments, JPMorgan says it has financed and facilitated more than $230 billion for industries covered by the initiative. Expansion by Kinexys by J.P. Morgan brings USD deposit token to Layer 1 blockchain network Kinexys by J.P. Morgan, the firm’s industry-leading blockchain business unit and part of J.P. Morgan Payments, has brought JPM Coin (ticker: JPMD), J.P. Morgan’s USD-denominated deposit token, to Ethereum, the Layer 1 blockchain network. Available to J.P. Morgan’s institutional clients, the move extends the reach of institutional finance on public blockchain. Large institutions that actively participate in both crypto and real-world-asset (RWA) digital transactions are increasingly looking for native onchain cash solutions from pre-eminent and reputable financial institutions that are interoperable with the deposit-based products they already use. Ethereum's established depth of onchain liquidity and tokenized assets makes it a natural next public blockchain for JPM Coin. Institutional clients can now move money quickly, easily and securely on Ethereum in addition to Base – the Ethereum Layer 2 blockchain – meaningfully expanding the scale of access to native onchain cash that sits alongside the assets, collateral, and counterparties they transact with already. JPM Coin joins a growing set of J.P. Morgan tokenized offerings on Ethereum, following the launch of J.P. Morgan Asset Management's tokenized money market funds on the network earlier this year. Matthew Dawson, Co-Founder of Ethereum Institutional, said, "We're delighted to see J.P. Morgan Payments bring JPM Coin to Ethereum. It builds on a clear trajectory: JPM Coin is already live on Base, J.P. Morgan Asset Management has tokenized money market funds on Ethereum, and the Kinexys platform itself is built on Ethereum Virtual Machine technology. J.P. Morgan Payments’ choice reflects what Ethereum uniquely offers institutions: unmatched liquidity depth, tokenized assets, applications, and security as the most proven public blockchain. It's a clear signal that institutional finance is moving onto public, verifiable infrastructure." Emma Landriault, Global Head of Kinexys Labs at Kinexys by J.P. Morgan, said, “Tokenized financial infrastructure is no longer theoretical. It’s already restructuring liquidity, settlement, and digital asset workflows. Issuing JPM Coin first on Base and now on Ethereum is a meaningful step towards providing our institutional clients with multi-chain optionality for moving wholesale money across both the web3 and traditional finance ecosystems.” As a deposit token, JPM Coin, launched in November 2025, supports peer-to-peer transfers between institutional clients within the Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM) ecosystem, including Base and Ethereum, providing a new, resilient onchain base liquidity layer for USD deposits. This reduces friction while enabling the potential for programmable treasury out of institutional clients’ wallet interfaces and can help institutions make faster, more informed and automated financial decisions, while streamlining onchain digital asset transactions. JPMorgan has expanded the reach of its JPM Coin, making the token available to institutional clients on the Ethereum mainnet as of October 19, 2026. The move, reported by CoinDesk, follows the initial launch of the token on the Coinbase-linked layer-2 network Base in November 2025 and marks a shift in how the bank approaches wholesale money movement on public infrastructure. It is necessary to distinguish JPM Coin from the broader category of retail-facing stablecoins. JPM Coin is a permissioned USD deposit token, functioning as a 1:1 representation of dollar deposits held at JPMorgan. Access is strictly limited to approved institutional counterparties through the bank's Kinexys platform, formerly Onyx. This structure ensures that the token remains a tool for wholesale settlement rather than a freely circulating asset. The decision to deploy on Ethereum is driven by the network's scale. Nearly $50 billion in crypto assets are locked in Ethereum-based applications, per DeFiLlama. By moving onto the mainnet, JPMorgan is positioning its deposit token within an ecosystem that already hosts significant institutional activity and liquidity. This expansion broadens the bank's blockchain footprint beyond its private Kinexys network, which currently processes more than $7 billion in transactions daily, and the Base layer-2 network. Emma Landriault, head of Kinexys Labs at JPMorgan, framed the deployment as a strategic necessity for institutional clients. she told CoinDesk. This multi-chain approach suggests that the bank is prioritizing interoperability to meet the diverse technical requirements of its institutional base. The timing of this expansion is notable given the approaching January 18, 2027, effective date of the GENIUS Act. As regulatory requirements tighten, financial institutions are under pressure to establish verifiable production track records for their digital asset initiatives. JPM Coin on a public mainnet provides a high-visibility environment to demonstrate the operational viability of tokenized deposits under real-world conditions, and it does so while the bank's broader reserve layer buildout continues to take shape. JPMorgan is not acting in isolation. The bank is among more than 30 institutions collaborating with Swift to define the governance and features of a blockchain-based ledger. A coalition of major U.S. banks, including Citi, Bank of America, and Wells Fargo, has signaled intentions to develop a shared network for tokenized deposits. Most still operate on private networks. JPMorgan's willingness to put its deposit token on a public mainnet is the differentiating move here. The infrastructure for institutional-grade stablecoin and deposit token payments is now being built in the open. With Visa, Mastercard, and now JPMorgan all shipping on production rails during Money20/20 week, the question is no longer whether public blockchains can serve institutional settlement. title: JPMorgan's JPM Coin Arrives on Ethereum, Putting Bank Dollars on a Public Blockchain - Decrypt

JPMorgan's JPM Coin Arrives on Ethereum, Putting Bank Dollars on a Public Blockchain JPMorgan Chase is putting JPM Coin on Ethereum, which gives its biggest clients a way to move dollars in seconds on a Sunday night as easily as on a Tuesday morning. A normal wire between banks only moves during business hours and can take days to land, which is why JPMorgan started experimenting with blockchain technology. The idea is using JPM Coin to cut that wait to seconds. The token is a deposit token, so each unit stands for a dollar already sitting in a JPMorgan account, and the bank's site says clients can redeem it for dollars at any time with no lock-up. A stablecoin, by contrast, is a token pegged to the dollar by a private company that holds the reserves somewhere else. Only vetted, approved counterparties can hold JPM Coin, so this is not a coin anyone can buy on an exchange. JPMorgan first put the token on Base, a cheaper and faster network built on top of Ethereum and incubated by Coinbase, in November 2025. That followed months of testing with Mastercard and Coinbase, and holders can now move the token between the two networks. In January, the bank also said it would bring JPM Coin to Canton Network, a privacy-focused blockchain built for financial markets. It has also issued two tokenized money-market funds on Ethereum, in December 2025 and May 2026, which are funds holding short-term debt that are represented as tokens. Emma Landriault, global head of Kinexys Labs at JPMorgan's blockchain unit, pointed to the money and tokenized assets (traditional investments such as shares, debt and funds, issued as blockchain tokens) already circulating on Ethereum, where about $50 billion sits in applications, according to DefiLlama. Crypto firms are expected to use the token for payments, while financial institutions can use it to pay for trades in tokenized assets or to post collateral, meaning a guarantee against a deal. “We’ve clearly been in a year of further convergence between Wall Street and crypto,” Landriault told Bloomberg. Matthew Dawson, co-founder of Ethereum Institutional, called the move “a clear signal that institutional finance is moving onto public, verifiable infrastructure.” Bitmine Immersion Technologies kept its weekly Ethereum buying streak alive, adding 12,535 ETH worth about $30 million, even as a market-wide selloff battered crypto prices and the firm closed in on the end of its accumulation.
The NYSE-listed company said Monday its holdings now total 6,041,481 ETH, valued at roughly $14.3 billion at a reference price of $2,365 per coin. That represents 4.9% of Ethereum’s 122.1 million token supply, leaving Bitmine, by its own count, 99% of the way to its goal... The bank is also fighting for the same customers as stablecoin issuers. A consortium of more than 100 companies including Visa, Stripe, and Mastercard launched its own dollar stablecoin last month, while Kinexys co-head Naveen Mallela has said deposit tokens are “a compelling alternative” to stablecoins because they “can be yield-bearing,” meaning they can pay interest. Kinexys, the unit behind the token, has handled more than $4 trillion in cumulative transactions and averages about $7 billion a day, against roughly $12 trillion a day across JPMorgan's wider payments business. JPMorgan, Citigroup and other large banks plan to launch a shared 24/7 tokenized deposit network as early as the first half of 2027. title: JPMorgan Expands JPM Coin to Ethereum for Tokenized Transfers - PaymentsJournal
content: As an early adopter of digital assets, JPMorgan is now positioned to build on its substantial infrastructure. After bringing its USD-backed deposit token, JPM Coin (JPMD), to the Base blockchain last year, the bank is launching the institution-focused token on Ethereum. Despite the “coin” in its name, JPMD is a unit of account for tokenized deposits—not a stablecoin. It represents deposits held at JPMorgan on a public blockchain, allowing institutional clients to make on-chain payments with greater speed and efficiency. Bringing JPMD to Ethereum, one of the most established blockchains, could expand the token’s reach and potential use cases. This expansion highlights the growing distinction between stablecoins and tokenized deposits. While both represent fiat currency in digital form, stablecoins are typically issued by private companies and backed by reserves. Tokenized deposits, by contrast, represent funds held at regulated banks, a key reason major banks have increasingly favored this approach. Several leading U.S. banks, including JPMorgan Chase, are planning to launch their own bank-led tokenized deposit network. Unlike some of its peers, JPMorgan has invested in digital assets for years. At the center of its efforts is Kinexys, one of the first blockchain platforms developed by a financial institution. The platform has evolved to support a range of functions aimed at streamlining global financial services through digital assets, including bank-to-bank transfers and foreign exchange conversions. JPMorgan recently expanded Kinexys’ foreign exchange capabilities. Last year, the bank also launched its first tokenized money-market fund on Ethereum through the platform. According to the Block, Kinexys has facilitated more than $4 trillion in transactions to date, with an average daily transaction volume of $7 billion. As tokenized deposits offer institutions new ways to streamline and automate transfers, their use could continue to grow, especially among firms engaged in foreign exchange and treasury management. Integrating JPM Coin into these transactions could further expand Kinexys’ role in institutional payments and cross-border finance. title: J.P. Morgan Team Departs to Create $18.6B Independent Firm - Wealth Management
content: Phil Scott and Jim Atwood are forming Latigo Peak Partners, launching with 48 employees and a presence in Florida, Washington, Massachusetts and California. An advisory duo who managed about $18.6 billion in client assets at J.P. Morgan Advisors is going independent with the launch of Latigo Peak Partners. Phil Scott and Jim Atwood founded the RIA to work with ultra-high-net-worth individuals and families. It is based in Palm Beach Gardens, Fla., with co-operational hubs in Bellevue, Wash., and Boston, as well as a field office in Los Angeles. With its launch, the firm immediately became one of the country’s largest independent wealth firms. It remains founder-owned and self-funded, without any private equity capital, and intends to follow a long-term vision rather than manage for a future transaction. Currently, SEC records list 10 registrants affiliated with the firm. In addition to the founders, 48 professionals are with Latigo Peak at its launch. According to Scott, Latigo Peak Partners’ goal is to “build a firm geared principally toward investment performance and a distinctive client experience,” and that “independence gives us the ability to take responsibility for the future of our business and make decisions based on what we believe is right for our clients over the long term.” Related:Deals & Moves: WPCG-Backed Apella, Waverly Keep Acquiring According to SEC records, Atwood was with Merrill Lynch from 1984 to 2018, when he joined First Republic Wealth Management (which was subsequently bought by JPMorgan following the regional bank crisis spurred by Silicon Valley Bank’s collapse in 2022). At J.P. Morgan Advisors, Scott and Atwood led two wealth management practices and, over the past six years, grew their total revenue from $34 million to $130 million. The new firm follows a family capital model, employing investment performance and comprehensive planning to meet individual family needs, without requiring families to fit a predetermined institutional model. The services include assessments of individual income requirements, risk tolerance, liquidity needs and long-term objectives, and the firm will build customized portfolios with family-office-style services, including estate and wealth planning and philanthropic advice. Latigo Peak will custody with Charles Schwab and BNY Pershing, with Fusion Financial Partners acting as a strategic advisor for the firm’s launch. title: JPMD Reaches Base for Institutional On-Chain Cash - TradingView
content: The biggest Ethereum news of the day comes from Wall Street, not from a developer call. JPMorgan is taking JPM Coin (JPMD), its tokenized dollar deposit, from Base to Ethereum mainnet. Kinexys, the bank’s blockchain unit, said in a statement on Monday that JPMD now supports transfers across Ethereum Virtual Machine networks, including Base and Ethereum. Access stays the same. JPMD is for approved institutional clients only, so there is no new coin for retail to buy. What changes is where the bank’s money can move. News: JPM Coin (JPMD), @jpmorgan's USD deposit token, is now live on @ethereum. JPMD extends from Base to Ethereum L1, giving institutional clients native onchain cash that sits alongside the assets, collateral and counterparties they transact with already. EXCLUSIVE: Unlock AI Trading Strategies and Best Crypto AI Trading Bots With BloFin Liquidity. Kinexys pointed to Ethereum’s “established depth of onchain liquidity and tokenized assets” as the reason it was the natural next chain. Emma Landriault, global head of Kinexys Labs, told Bloomberg that crypto firms could use JPMD for payments, while financial institutions could use it to settle trades or post collateral against tokenized assets. Tokenized financial infrastructure is no longer theoretical The bank has been building toward this for a while. JPMD went live on Base, Coinbase’s Ethereum layer 2, in November 2025 after a pilot that started in June, with Coinbase, Mastercard and B2C2 testing issuance and redemption. JPMorgan then launched its first tokenized money-market fund on Ethereum in December 2025 and a second, JLTXX, in May. In January, Digital Asset and Kinexys said JPMD would also come natively to the Canton Network during 2026. For context, Kinexys says it has processed more than $4 trillion since launch and averages about $7 billion a day. That covers the whole platform, so it says nothing about JPMD alone. JPMorgan hasn’t disclosed how much JPMD is in circulation, and the statement came without a mainnet contract address or a go-live date. JPMD is a bank deposit in token form. Each token is a claim on US dollars held at JPMorgan, with the bank’s balance sheet behind it, and it can pay interest. A stablecoin like USDC is a separate asset issued by a separate company and backed by a reserve. That difference is the whole pitch. Kara Kennedy, global co-head of Kinexys, said at the Singapore Fintech Festival last November that tokenized deposits get clearer capital and accounting treatment than newer forms of digital money. Banks can book them like any other deposit. The token is also permissioned. Clients hold it through Blockchain Deposit Accounts, and only approved clients can receive or move it, even on a chain as open as Ethereum. So why put it on a public chain at all? Money that runs around the clock and can be programmed. Kennedy pointed to Kinexys’s intraday repo product, where a repo can be opened and closed down to the minute. A repo is a short-term loan: one side hands over assets for cash and agrees to swap them back later. Cutting that cycle from days to minutes frees up cash banks would otherwise park as a buffer. Kennedy doesn’t expect the old rails to vanish. She sees public and private blockchains running next to existing bank systems for years, possibly decades, but expects tokenized finance to look very different within five to 10 years. Transfer rules for regulated digital tokens illustrate how compliance requirements can be built into token infrastructure. Not much today. ETH trades at $2,423, up 0.14% over 24 hours but down 4.94% on the week, and the Ethereum news barely registered on the chart. JPMD transfers pay gas in ETH like any other transaction, but the token itself won’t sit in anyone’s retail portfolio. The longer story is demand for blockspace. Almost $50 billion is already locked in Ethereum apps, according to DefiLlama, and every bank that settles on mainnet strengthens the case that Ethereum is where tokenized finance lives. On the daily chart, ETH sits between its 50-day exponential moving average (EMA) at $2,483.81 and its 200-day EMA at $2,314.14. A daily close above the 50-day puts $2,546.66 in view. Lose $2,371 and the 200-day EMA is next. Wall Street is coming onchain one deposit at a time. The price may take longer to notice. title: Digging into the rare opportunity in muni bonds today - J.P. Morgan Private Bank
content: The Private Bank’s mission is to build, preserve & transform our client’s wealth. We work with a variety of clients to help them achieve their unique ambitions. Our world-class economists, strategists, and investment specialists share their timely ideas and perspectives. We have worked with clients for more than 200 years to help them achieve their unique ambitions. Three forces are converging to make municipal bonds very appealing today: Higher yields, heavier supply and the simple math of taxes. Real yields for munis are currently at their highest levels since 2020, when the market was being upended by the COVID-19 pandemic. That creates an opportunity to use high-quality munis to lock in more attractive, tax-efficient income. With that in mind, we see opportunity in munis for U.S. taxable investors heading into Q4. For most taxable U.S. investors, the appeal of municipal bonds is enduring: They provide steady income and meaningful tax advantages via the tax-exempt status of the income received. Munis have long played a stabilizing role in portfolios, but they’ve often been overlooked relative to equities and other investments. That’s changed dramatically in 2026; therefore, we think they deserve another look. This year, bonds have sold off and yields have risen as markets repriced the path of policy rates amid higher energy prices, heavier global borrowing needs and more-hawkish central banks. It’s one of the largest bond market moves in recent decades.1 This wave of falling bond prices and rising yields intensified in September, when benchmark U.S. Treasury bond yields hit their highest levels in more than 20 years. For munis, the move was amplified by elevated issuance from state and local borrowers. In September, it caused muni prices to underperform Treasury bond prices—an unusual dynamic that creates an opportunity to lock in higher muni yields. Source: Bloomberg Finance L.P. FactSet, J.P. In our view, these higher yields have reset the risk-reward tradeoff in a way that long-term investors rarely see, especially in high-quality fixed income. Importantly, the repricing has been driven primarily by higher rates and not a broad deterioration in the essential services munis help finance. Investors can potentially get more income today for taking high-quality duration risk than they have in years Even if we continue to see short-term volatility in bond prices, a higher starting yield can make a big difference. Locking in higher tax-exempt income today can support returns over time via compounding interest without requiring perfect rate timing. Here, we’ll explain why this combination of timely factors and municipal bond characteristics creates a highly appealing environment for bond investors. State and local governments issue muni bonds to finance critical infrastructure and other needs. Municipal bonds not only fund specialty projects, but they also fund the backbone of local economies, like water and sewer systems, schools, roads and bridges, hospitals, transit and public power. If you’ve ever turned on the tap, driven on a toll road, dropped kids at a public school, or walked into a local hospital, you’ve relied on what muni bonds help build. In a very real sense, most Americans already live like muni investors. The income from municipal bonds is exempt from federal taxes, including the 3.8% Medicare surtax on net investment income (or NIIT). In many cases, it’s exempt from state taxes as well.2 While munis have lower nominal, or pre-tax, yields, the after-tax income is what should matter most to potential and current investors. An individual’s tax rate makes a significant difference, particularly for residents of high-tax states. That’s why the right comparison for munis is not “yield vs. yield,” but “after-tax income vs. after-tax income.”3 This after-tax income, also known as tax-equivalent yield, is used to estimate what a taxable bond would need to yield to match a muni’s after-tax income. The chart below compares the tax-equivalent yields of AAA grade and BBB grade munis to U.S. Treasury bonds. The additional yield from munis reflects their tax benefits and the additional risk compared to Treasuries, while the following two charts show the fiscal health of U.S. municipalities compared to the federal government and the corporate sector. Essential-service revenue streams (like water/sewer), conservative debt service coverage, strong reserves and manageable pension/OPEB trends are things we look for and are especially important when reaching for longer maturities. While muni bonds are theoretically riskier than Treasuries, which are regarded as the safest investments available, defaults are very rare at the highest-rated levels. According to Moody’s, the 10-year default rate for AAA rated muni bonds is 0.0%, and for AA rated munis, it’s 0.2%.4 In our view, today’s environment rewards an up-in-quality approach because it is possible to capture higher yields without needing to compromise on credit standards. There are three main ways to access munis, each with its own trade-offs. Individual bonds give you direct ownership of specific securities, with a known maturity date and coupon, which appeals to investors who want full control and a predictable, bond-by-bond cash flow schedule. An investor could pick their own muni bonds to invest in their own brokerage account. Separately managed accounts (SMAs) are portfolios of individual bonds built and managed by a financial professional. Like owning bonds directly, SMAs typically offer defined maturities and cash flows, which many investors find appealing when the goal is reliable, tax-efficient income, but with professional selection and ongoing oversight. The trade-off is that, depending on account size and mandate, diversification may be narrower than a pooled vehicle. ETFs offer broad diversification, daily liquidity and quick implementation. The trade-off is that you own shares of a pooled portfolio rather than specific bonds held to maturity, so your cash flows and tax outcomes will behave differently than they would with direct ownership. Several states have recently passed laws that either increase their top marginal tax rates or create a new personal income tax on high earners. If tax rates rise further, the value of tax-exempt income can become even more pronounced. Municipal bonds can potentially provide tax-efficient income, portfolio stability, and diversification, but the right approach depends on your tax profile, state of residence, time horizon and liquidity needs. title: Ethereum hosts JPM Coin for institutional payments - Cointribune
content: JPMorgan extends JPM Coin directly to Ethereum. Its dollar deposit token, JPMD, was already available on Base since November 2025. It can now be used by approved institutional clients on the Ethereum network to make payments, settle transactions on tokenized assets, or move collateral. Kinexys has already processed over 4 trillion dollars since its launch. JPMorgan had already deployed JPM Coin on Base, Coinbase’s Layer 2 in November 2025. The bank now adds Ethereum itself. The choice is notably based on the depth of available liquidity on the network and the amount of already tokenized financial assets. JPM Coin, whose ticker is JPMD, represents dollar deposits held at JPMorgan. An institutional client can therefore convert part of their bank deposit into tokens, transfer them on blockchain, and then convert them back. Transactions can be carried out in a few seconds, including outside traditional banking hours. Emma Landriault, Global Head of Kinexys Labs, explains that crypto companies will notably be able to use JPMD for their on-chain payments. Financial institutions, on their side, will be able to settle transactions or post collateral. However, JPMD remains reserved for clients approved by JPMorgan. Ethereum thus becomes public for the infrastructure, but access to the token remains controlled. JPM Coin is not JPMorgan’s first operation on Ethereum. In December 2025, the bank had already launched MONY, its tokenized money market fund on Ethereum. The product started with 100 million dollars provided by JPMorgan and allows qualified investors to gain exposure to short-term debt securities directly on-chain. A second tokenized fund followed in May. The movement therefore goes beyond simple payments. Ethereum begins to bring together on the same infrastructure tokenized bank money, money market funds, stablecoins, and other real-world assets. JPM Coin notably brings an important piece: the cash needed for settlement. An institution can for example purchase a tokenized asset and use a also tokenized JPMorgan deposit to settle the transaction. Both legs of the operation can then operate on blockchain infrastructures. Kinexys has grown considerably in the meantime. JPMorgan indicates that its blockchain platform has exceeded 4 trillion dollars in cumulative transactions. Its average daily volume now hovers around 7 billion dollars. In April, the bank still spoke of over 3 trillion cumulative and about 5 billion dollars per day. The growth is rapid. JPMD looks very much like a stablecoin on the surface. One token represents one dollar and can circulate on a public blockchain. The legal structure is different. JPM Coin represents a bank deposit at JPMorgan. The user must therefore be a client of the bank and meet its eligibility criteria. USDC or USDT, on the other hand, can circulate between wallets without each holder having an account with their partner bank. JPMorgan is experimenting with several networks for this model. After Base and Ethereum, the bank also plans to extend JPM Coin to Canton Network, an infrastructure particularly oriented toward institutional financial markets. The arrival on Ethereum remains symbolic however. JPMorgan long favored its own private blockchain infrastructures. It now directly uses public networks for certain financial products while retaining control over authorized users. The Ethereum network therefore does not simply host a new dollar token. title: $18.6 Billion J.P. Morgan Teams Led by Phil Scott, Atwood Launch RIA - AdvisorHub
content: Two top-producing J.P. Morgan Advisors teams led by Phil Scott and Jim Atwood broke away on Friday to launch their own RIA, according to an announcement. Scott and Atwood oversaw a combined $18.6 billion and generated $130 million in revenue, according to the announcement. They have self-funded the launch of Latigo Peak Partners and are the two primary owners of the RIA through a holding company, ASO Meridian Holdings, according to the announcement. The Palm Beach Gardens, Florida-based firm has 48 employees and offices in Bellevue, Washington, as well as Boston and Los Angeles. It will use Charles Schwab & Co. and BNY’s Pershing Advisor Solutions for custody and lending, according to the announcement. Two sources close to the team said that Scott and Atwood had been frustrated by the technology and bureaucracy at J.P. Morgan. They likely forfeited substantial deferred compensation and must repay unvested balances on their forgivable recruiting loans granted when they joined a predecessor. “Nothing to do with money,” one of the sources said of the team’s reasons for moving. “They were square pegs in a round hole.” The duo touted in the announcement that their combined revenue had nearly quadrupled from $34 million over the past six years. Scott and Atwood became J.P. Morgan advisors following its parent bank’s purchase of First Republic’s assets out of government receivership in 2023. The name Latigo is tied to a ski run in Beaver Creek, Colorado, and one of the sources noted their close ties to a group of senior advisors who have met regularly in the ski town, for about two decades. A J.P. Morgan spokesperson did not immediately return a request for comment. Dozens of First Republic brokers left in the year following the acquisition. The brokerage unit has around 600 brokers and is a fraction of JPMorgan Chase & Co.’s wealth division. Scott and Atwood each started their careers at Merrill in 1984 and went on to rank among its top five producers. Scott had also managed the personal wealth of other advisors at Merrill as well as their clients. Latigo manages nine in-house investment strategies and participates as a separate-account manager on Schwab’s Managed Account Marketplace, according to regulatory filings. Outside RIAs and family offices will be able to hire it while maintaining their client relationships. The release did not specify how much of the $18.6 billion is subadvised. Latigo also pays accountants a flat fee or an ongoing percentage of advisory revenue for client referrals. Scott, who is registered as Walter P. Schlaepfer, joined First Republic in Bellevue in 2020 with an 11-person team that had generated around $18 million in revenue and oversaw $2.7 billion in client assets. In the past five years, Scott has made headlines over his political donations and mixed success in clearing customer complaints from his public record. Atwood joined First Republic in 2018 in Boston with a 15-person team that generated $22 million in revenue and oversaw $4.5 billion in assets. He has no disclosures or client complaints on his record. Neither remains registered as a broker with the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority. The two hired Fusion Financial Partners, a recruiting firm founded by former Hightower Advisors executives, to advise them on founding the RIA. title: JPMorgan brings JPM Coin, representing dollar deposits, to Ethereum - CoinDesk
content:
JPMorgan(JPM), the largest U.S. bank, brought its almost year-old crypto token, JPM Coin, to Ethereum as part of a plan to expand beyond Base, the layer-2 blockchain built by Coinbase Global COIN$168.31·Market Closed. JPM Coin, which represents dollar deposits at the bank, was technically deployed on the Ethereum mainnet on Monday and is available for institutional clients’ use, the bank said in an emailed statement. The bank chose Ethereum because the blockchain offers more liquidity than rival networks and is already used by institutional clients, Emma Landriault, the head of Kinexys Labs at JPMorgan’s blockchain division Kinexys, said in an interview with Bloomberg, which reported the news earlier. “Issuing JPM Coin first on Base and now on Ethereum is a meaningful step towards providing our institutional clients with multi-chain optionality for moving wholesale money across both the web3 and traditional finance ecosystems,” she said in the emailed statement. The banking giant flagged a move outside Base back in January, saying it was planning to take the token to the Canton Network. Broadening its availability aims to serve crypto firms that want to make blockchain payments and financial firms that need a digital token to settle trades or back tokenized assets, Landriault said. Tokenization is the process of converting real-world assets and financial assets into a digital form that’s recorded and traded on a decentralized ledger. The advantage is speed, including faster settlement of trades, quick movement of money while bypassing delays and frictions involved in traditional rails. Banks have embraced tokenization, but mostly away from public networks. In the U.S., JPMorgan, Citi (C), Bank of America (BAC) and Wells Fargo (WFC), along with more than a dozen other banks, have plans to start a shared network for tokenized deposits. JPMorgan’s private blockchain network, Kinexys, already handles more than $7 billion a day, a small piece in the bank’s $12 trillion a day payments business. Almost $50 billion worth of crypto assets are locked in Ethereum-based applications, according to DeFiLlama. Abroad, JPMorgan is among more than 30 banks that are helping Swift, the interbank messaging service, define the features and governance of its blockchain-based ledger. In July, Swift said 17 banks, including Citi and Wells Fargo, were preparing to pilot live transactions on it. JPMorgan wasn’t on that list. JPMorgan is bringing its JPM Coin deposit token to Ethereum for institutional clients, Bloomberg reported. Commentator Borovik's $60,000 ETH scenario has drawn criticism over its reliance on stablecoin transfer volumes. The forecast goes beyond bullish calls covered by CCN, including $10,000 ETH commentary backed by Tom Lee and Standard Chartered's $40,000 outlook. JPMorgan is bringing its JPM Coin deposit token to Ethereum for institutional clients, according to Bloomberg, extending a product initially launched on Base. Its expansion into Ethereum has led some bulls to celebrate its institutional adoption story, as a $60,000 ETH prediction draws scrutiny of how much that growth could benefit token holders. Leading the bulls is crypto commentator Borovik, who pointed to Ethereum's role in stablecoin payments as a reason Ethereum could rise roughly 25-fold. But critics argue his calculations leave a crucial question unanswered: how does money moving across Ethereum translate into a higher price for ETH? JPMorgan's deposit token represents dollar deposits at the bank, allowing eligible institutional customers to transfer money on blockchain infrastructure around the clock. According to Bloomberg's reporting, the Ethereum expansion announced on Oct. 19 targets large crypto businesses that make payments and financial institutions seeking digital cash to settle transactions. Emma Landriault, global head of Kinexys Labs, told Bloomberg that ETH's liquidity and its existing use among clients influenced the bank's decision. "We've clearly been in a year of further convergence between Wall Street and crypto," Landriault said. "It's not just Wall Street going to public chains, but the institutional web3 players getting more embedded and partnering with traditional financial institutions." The move builds on JPM Coin's rollout on Base, an Ethereum layer-2 network, last year. It expands the bank's public blockchain presence, although eligibility restrictions mean the token is not available to all Ethereum users. In an Oct. 18 post on X, Borovik outlined a bullish scenario based on Ethereum's position in the stablecoin market. He cited more than $20 trillion in ETH stablecoin transfers over the 12 months through June 2026, attributing the figure to Fidelity, and put the network's share of global stablecoin supply at approximately 48%. He then applied that percentage to Citi's projection of roughly $100 trillion in annual stablecoin transaction activity by 2030. "If ETH captures 48% of flows: ~$48T/year," Borovik wrote. In a follow-up, he described the $60,000 scenario as "a 25x from current prices." Citi's research projects nearly $100 trillion in annual stablecoin activity under its base case. However, that estimate depends on several assumptions, including stablecoin issuance and the frequency with which tokens change hands. Responses to Borovik's post challenged the connection between those payment flows and ETH's valuation. "Transfer volume isn't the same as value accruing to ETH, though," wrote one user. Another user, going by SlopMachine, offered a sharper analogy: "Valuing the toll booth by adding up the cash inside passing armored trucks." The calculation yields a potential transfer volume figure, but it does not establish a $60,000 token price. First, Ethereum hosting 48% of the stablecoin supply would not necessarily mean it processes 48% of transfers. Tokens on different networks can move at different speeds and frequencies. Second, transfer volume measures the amount of money changing hands. The same dollars can be transferred repeatedly, increasing the annual total without a corresponding increase in invested capital. Third, ETH's transaction fees depend on computational work and demand for network capacity, rather than a fixed percentage of the dollars being moved. title: JPMorgan Expands JPM Coin to Ethereum for Institutional Payments - Coinpedia
content: JPMorgan’s decision to bring JPM Coin (JPMD) to Ethereum adds another network to the bank’s blockchain operations, raising a broader question about how financial institutions will manage digital money across different blockchains. The US dollar deposit token launched on Base in November 2025. Its Ethereum expansion gives eligible institutional clients another network for transferring bank deposits, while JPMorgan continues developing blockchain-based financial products across its business. The move is not a shift away from Base. Instead, it extends JPM Coin’s reach to Ethereum, where JPMorgan already has tokenized money market funds, including MONY and JLTXX. This move highlights how banks are exploring multiple blockchain networks rather than relying on a single platform for every financial product. Base provided the initial public blockchain network for JPM Coin. Ethereum now adds access to a separate ecosystem of tokenized assets and financial applications. JPMorgan has also explored native JPM Coin issuance on Canton, according to previously announced plans reported by PrimeXBT. This approach allows the bank to develop its blockchain services around different institutional requirements. However, operating across multiple networks does not automatically mean assets or deposits can move freely between them. Each deployment depends on its own technical setup, access rules and integration arrangements. JPMorgan’s Ethereum presence includes both investment products and its newly expanded deposit token, but the two serve different purposes. MONY and JLTXX represent interests in tokenized money market funds. JPM Coin, by contrast, represents US dollar deposits held at JPMorgan and is intended for payments and institutional transactions. Having these products on the same network creates potential for closer integration. However, JPMorgan has not confirmed that all subscriptions, redemptions or settlements for its tokenized funds will use JPM Coin. The distinction matters because issuing financial products on a blockchain is only one part of building a complete digital financial system. Institutions must also establish how money moves, how transactions are settled and which participants can access the services. JPMorgan’s Ethereum deployment establishes another option for institutional clients, but the wider impact will depend on actual usage. Key indicators include the volume of transactions conducted through JPM Coin on Ethereum, the number of participating institutions and whether the network supports new integrations with tokenized financial products. Until those figures become available, the expansion is best understood as an extension of JPMorgan’s blockchain infrastructure rather than evidence that institutional finance has moved away from traditional banking systems. JPMorgan remains the issuer of the deposit token, and access is restricted to eligible institutional clients. Ethereum provides another network for its use, while the bank continues to control the banking relationship and participation requirements.  kicked off the US banking reporting season this week with a quarterly update that drew wide attention across markets, posting record revenue as a revival in dealmaking and a surge in equity trading more than offset a softer patch in bond trading. The largest American bank by assets has long served as a bellwether for the health of the wider financial system, and the latest set of figures reinforced that role. Revenue climbed from the prior-year period, lifted by robust fee generation across the firm's banking franchise and steady lending activity across its consumer and commercial arms. The report arrived during a week dominated by questions over delayed economic data, the path of interest rates and the tone of commentary from the Federal Reserve. Against that backdrop, the strength of the bank's capital-markets engine stood out. Market participants had been watching closely to see whether a pickup in merger activity and capital raising earlier in the year would translate into firmer fee revenue, and the quarter offered an affirmative signal that the dealmaking cycle has regained momentum. The standout theme was the rebound across the firm's markets and banking businesses. Equity trading revenue jumped sharply as elevated volumes and volatility across global exchanges kept desks busy, while advisory and underwriting fees benefited from a healthier pipeline of mergers, acquisitions and debt issuance. Corporate clients returned to the capital markets in greater numbers, and the bank's scale allowed it to capture a meaningful slice of that renewed activity. Rates and credit trading, by contrast, cooled compared with the unusually active conditions seen a year earlier, a pattern echoed across several peers. Even so, the breadth of the franchise meant that the softness in bond trading was comfortably absorbed by the strength elsewhere. The combination underscored a familiar advantage: a diversified mix of businesses that can lean on one engine when another slows. Beyond the trading floor, the core lending machine remained a central pillar of the quarterly update. Net interest earnings, the spread the bank captures between what it charges on loans and what it pays on deposits, held up well even as the rate environment shifted. Loan balances across cards, commercial lending and wholesale banking stayed resilient, and deposit trends steadied after an extended period of migration toward higher-yielding accounts. The firm has guided that the spread between lending and funding costs can stay supportive as the rate path evolves, helped by disciplined pricing and a vast, sticky deposit base. That balance between market-sensitive fee revenue and steadier lending earnings is a defining feature of the franchise, and it was again on display in the latest numbers. Credit quality is always a focal point when a lender of this size reports, because its books offer an early read on the financial health of American families and companies. This week's update pointed to credit trends that remained broadly contained. Charge-offs across the card business ticked along in line with normalization rather than deterioration, and reserves were adjusted to reflect a still-uncertain economic picture rather than any sharp downturn. The bank continued to build a cushion against softer patches in the economy while signaling that borrowers, on the whole, were managing repayment obligations. Commercial real estate and lower-rated consumer segments stayed on the watch list, as they have for several quarters, but the overall message leaned toward stability rather than stress. Few names carry as much weight in the financial sector as this one. As a member of the S&P 500 and a heavyweight within the broader banking group, the company's results ripple across the perceptions that market participants form about the entire industry. When it reports first each quarter, its commentary on lending demand, deposit behavior and capital-markets activity frames how the rest of the sector is read. For readers tracking the broader group of US Financial Stocks, the bank's scale across consumer banking, commercial banking, asset management and global markets makes it a useful lens on the cycle. Its sheer reach means the themes it flags, from dealmaking appetite to credit normalization, tend to surface across smaller peers in the weeks that follow. The competitive map in American banking continues to tilt toward scale. The largest firms, with their deep technology budgets, diversified revenue streams and sprawling client relationships, have steadily extended their reach, and this week's update reinforced how much ground the biggest players can cover. Rivals across money-center banking, regional lending and independent advisory houses all compete for slices of the same corporate and consumer wallets. At the same time, nimble financial-technology entrants and private-credit firms keep reshaping the edges of the market, pressing traditional lenders to keep modernizing payments, digital banking and wealth platforms. The bank has leaned heavily into technology spending to defend and extend its franchise, a theme that resurfaced in the latest commentary as management described ongoing modernization across its platforms. The wider economic environment framed this week's report in important ways. A delayed release of consumer price data and a steady stream of commentary from Federal Reserve officials kept the rate path at the front of market thinking. Banks sit directly in the crosscurrents of those rate decisions, since the spread between lending rates and deposit costs moves with the central bank's stance. A gradual easing in rates can compress lending spreads over time, yet it can also revive loan demand, support asset prices and encourage the kind of corporate activity that fuels dealmaking fees. The bank's diversified model means it can benefit from several of those channels at once, which is part of why its reports are parsed so closely for clues about the direction of the broader economy. Capital strength remained a recurring theme. The bank continued to operate with robust capital ratios well above regulatory minimums, giving it flexibility to support lending, absorb market swings and distribute capital to owners through dividends and buybacks. Management reiterated a disciplined stance on expenses even as the firm keeps spending heavily on technology, data capabilities and talent. Cost discipline matters in a period when revenue growth can be uneven across quarters. By keeping a tight rein on expenses while still funding long-term modernization, the firm aims to protect its efficiency even as it absorbs the swings that come with market-sensitive businesses. That balance between spending for growth and guarding margins was a notable thread in the latest commentary. The consumer and community banking arm, which serves millions of customers across cards, deposits and home lending, continued to anchor the franchise with steady activity. The commercial and corporate banking division captured the rebound in advisory and underwriting work, while the markets unit rode the surge in equity trading. Asset and wealth management benefited from firm markets and continued inflows across its platforms. Each segment tells part of the same story: a franchise broad enough to lean on whichever engine is running hot at a given moment. That diversification has been a hallmark of the firm for years and was again central to how the quarter came together, with weakness in one corner offset by strength in another. No reading of the quarter would be complete without acknowledging the headwinds that hang over the sector. Regulatory capital requirements continue to evolve, and large banks must adapt to shifting rules on how much capital they keep against their assets. Compression in lending spreads during an easing cycle, softer loan demand in a slowing economy, and the steady encroachment of private credit all present challenges that management teams must navigate. Cyber threats, operational resilience and the heavy cost of staying current on technology add further pressure. The largest firms are generally better placed to absorb these demands than smaller rivals, but the burdens are real and recurring, and they shape how the entire group approaches the quarters ahead. The market response to the update reflected the balance of its contents. Record revenue and a revival in dealmaking were welcomed, while the softer patch in bond trading and caution around the economy tempered some of the enthusiasm. As the first major bank to report each cycle, the company often sets the tone for how peers are received in the days that follow. Trading in the stock through the week drew heavy attention as participants weighed the strength of the capital-markets rebound against the broader uncertainty over rates and growth. The reaction underscored how much weight the market places on this particular report as a gauge of the sector's health. The asset and wealth management arm adds a steadier, fee-based layer to the franchise, serving individuals and institutions across advisory, brokerage and money-management services. Revenue there tends to track the level of assets under supervision rather than the swings of trading, offering a more recurring stream that complements the firm's market-sensitive engines. Continued client inflows and firm markets supported the business during the quarter. Growing that durable revenue has been a deliberate strategy, helping smooth the volatility that comes with a diversified bank. As asset balances expand, the wealth and asset management operations supply a measure of ballast, and management again highlighted steady progress across the platform in the latest update. The business remains a meaningful part of how the firm balances market-driven and recurring sources of revenue. Technology spending has become one of the defining features of how the largest banks compete, and this firm has placed modernization at the center of its strategy. The company has poured heavily into cloud computing, data platforms, artificial intelligence and payments infrastructure, aiming to speed up product development, sharpen fraud detection and deepen the digital relationships that increasingly define consumer banking. The latest commentary underscored that the pace of that spending is not slowing. The payoff from technology shows up in several places at once: lower unit costs as more activity moves to digital channels, faster onboarding of new customers, and richer data that helps the firm price credit and tailor products. Management has framed this spending as essential to defending the franchise against both traditional rivals and newer financial-technology entrants, and the breadth of the effort reflects how central software has become to modern banking. Beyond lending and trading, the firm operates one of the largest payments and treasury-services businesses in the world, moving enormous sums for corporations, governments and financial institutions every day. That business generates steady, fee-based revenue that is less sensitive to the swings of markets, and it binds large clients tightly to the franchise through deeply embedded relationships. Payments scale also reinforces the firm's deposit base, since corporate clients keep sizable balances tied to their treasury operations. As commerce continues to move toward real-time, digital and cross-border flows, the firm's heavy spending on payments infrastructure positions it to capture a growing share of that activity. The combination of scale and technology in this quiet corner of the franchise is a meaningful, if often overlooked, source of durable revenue. The firm's reach extends well beyond the United States, with operations spanning major financial centers across Europe, Asia and Latin America. That global footprint gives it a vantage point on economic conditions around the world and allows it to serve multinational clients across borders, a capability that smaller rivals struggle to match. The breadth of that reach surfaced in commentary on cross-border dealmaking and trading flows. Global scale cuts both ways, exposing the firm to a wider array of economic, regulatory and geopolitical crosscurrents even as it broadens the base of revenue. Navigating different rate cycles, currency swings and regulatory regimes is a constant demand on management, yet the diversification that comes with it has long been a structural strength, helping steady results when any single region softens. Looking to the period ahead, several threads stand out for readers following the company. The durability of the dealmaking rebound will be central, since advisory and underwriting fees swing with corporate confidence and market conditions. The trajectory of net interest earnings as the rate path shifts, the pace of credit normalization across consumer books, and the firm's continued technology spending all merit attention. The broader question is whether the strength shown this week marks a durable upswing across the banking group or a single strong quarter shaped by favorable trading conditions. As the bellwether of the sector, this name will remain a reference point for how that question is answered in the months to come, keeping it firmly in the market's line of sight. title: JPMorgan brings JPM Coin to Ethereum for institutional payments - Crypto News
content: JPMorgan Chase has expanded its JPM Coin deposit token to the Ethereum mainnet, giving approved institutional clients another public blockchain for around-the-clock dollar transfers, securities settlement and collateral payments. According to an October 19 Bloomberg report, the bank is making JPM Coin available on Ethereum after launching the deposit token on Coinbase’s Base network in November 2025. The latest expansion gives eligible clients access to a network already used by financial institutions and cryptocurrency businesses for tokenized assets. JPM Coin, which carries the ticker JPMD, represents US dollar deposits held at JPMorgan. The token allows participating customers to transfer funds in seconds without waiting for conventional banking hours. News: JPM Coin (JPMD), @jpmorgan's USD deposit token, is now live on @ethereum.JPMD extends from Base to Ethereum L1, giving institutional clients native onchain cash that sits alongside the assets, collateral and counterparties they transact with already.J.P. Morgan has now… pic.twitter.com/fNYAGoT3Pb The launch is intended for institutional payments and settlement activity, not public cryptocurrency trading. JPMorgan will continue restricting access to approved customers even though the underlying blockchain is open to other users. JPMorgan’s Ethereum rollout follows nearly a year of activity on Base, the Ethereum Layer 2 network developed by Coinbase. In November 2025, the bank made JPMD available to institutional clients after completing a proof-of-concept that began in June. Coinbase, Mastercard and digital asset trading firm B2C2 participated in the testing process. The companies completed transactions involving the issuance and redemption of JPM Coin, demonstrating how dollar deposits could move between conventional banking infrastructure and blockchain wallets. JPMorgan described the service as supporting near-instant transfers and continuous settlement for qualified participants. At the time, crypto.news reported the Base launch, including the bank’s plans to support more public blockchain networks. The October Ethereum expansion follows that previously announced direction. Base and Ethereum mainnet are related but separate blockchain networks. Base processes transactions through its own Layer 2 infrastructure, while Ethereum mainnet operates as the underlying Layer 1 network. JPMorgan’s decision brings its deposit token directly onto Ethereum, where a range of investment products, tokenized securities and financial applications already operate. The bank has not disclosed how many customers will initially use JPMD on mainnet or how much of the token will be issued through the new deployment. In a statement distributed Monday, Kinexys described Ethereum’s established on-chain liquidity and tokenized asset activity as reasons for choosing the network. The bank’s public comments identify the existing institutional ecosystem as a factor in its decision. JPMorgan expects cryptocurrency businesses and traditional financial institutions to use JPM Coin for different types of transactions. Emma Landriault, global head of Kinexys Labs, told Bloomberg that cryptocurrency companies could use JPMD to make payments through blockchain infrastructure. Financial institutions could use the token to settle trades or provide collateral for transactions involving tokenized assets. Settlement refers to the completion of a financial transaction, when the asset and corresponding payment are delivered to the relevant parties. In conventional markets, different payment systems and operating schedules can complicate transactions that involve participants in several jurisdictions. Using tokenized bank deposits allows approved institutions to transfer a digital representation of money through compatible blockchain wallets. JPMorgan’s product combines those transfers with the bank’s existing deposit and payment arrangements. The bank’s official product documentation describes payments, collateral transfers and transaction settlement as supported uses of JPM Coin. Clients access the service through Blockchain Deposit Accounts, which connect ordinary bank balances with corresponding blockchain-based deposits. Under this arrangement, a qualifying customer can exchange eligible balances for JPMD and redeem the token through JPMorgan’s infrastructure. The bank manages the relationship between the digital token and the corresponding commercial bank deposit. The product is designed to support programmable transactions, allowing approved users to establish payment instructions that work with blockchain-based systems. Those capabilities could be used in transactions involving tokenized investment products, although access still depends on the relevant financial institutions and platforms. The Ethereum announcement does not identify a particular securities exchange or clearinghouse that has newly agreed to accept JPMD as collateral. It establishes the bank’s expansion to the network and describes the intended institutional applications. Ethereum allows users to send transactions, deploy applications and interact with smart contracts without requiring membership in a private banking network. JPM Coin operates under a different access model because it represents deposits issued by JPMorgan. The bank limits the token to approved institutional clients that satisfy its account and compliance requirements. The distinction separates JPMD from cryptocurrencies that anyone can purchase and transfer through ordinary public wallets. A token can operate on a public blockchain while retaining restrictions on who may legally or technically hold it. JPMorgan identifies JPM Coin as commercial bank money in tokenized form. Its value comes from the corresponding deposit obligation of JPMorgan, making the bank’s credit standing and the terms of the deposit relationship relevant to customers. The token is not a public stablecoin available for unrestricted circulation, even though both products can represent dollar-denominated value on a blockchain. JPMorgan’s documentation identifies deposit-account infrastructure and bank-managed redemption arrangements as central parts of the product. The bank’s original Base announcement described institutional customers as the intended participants. Its October Ethereum launch maintains that limitation rather than opening JPMD to ordinary cryptocurrency investors. JPMorgan’s public materials warn users to verify the official token contract details because unrelated assets may use similar names on blockchain networks. The documents available for this report did not establish an Ethereum mainnet contract address that could be independently checked against the October deployment. The bank has not released a mainnet transaction total, circulating JPMD balance or confirmed count of active Ethereum users in the announcements reviewed. JPMorgan had established a separate presence on Ethereum before bringing its deposit token to mainnet. In December 2025, the bank’s asset management business introduced its first tokenized money market fund on Ethereum, initially backed by $100 million of internal capital. The product was designed to give institutional investors access to a fund using blockchain-based records of ownership. The Ethereum money market launch covered an investment product, not JPM Coin itself. Money market fund tokens represent interests in an underlying investment portfolio, while JPMD represents qualifying commercial bank deposits. In May 2026, J.P. Morgan Asset Management introduced a second tokenized money market fund called JLTXX. The fund invests in government money market instruments and was designed with the reserve requirements of eligible stablecoin issuers in mind. According to the asset manager’s May 13 announcement, JPMorgan committed $100 million to the new fund at launch. Qualified investors could subscribe through the Morgan Money platform and receive tokenized fund interests at their blockchain addresses. The fund’s assets and investor eligibility rules are separate from JPM Coin’s deposit-token arrangements. Neither the launch investment nor the tokenized fund’s total assets should be counted as JPMD already circulating on Ethereum. JPMorgan’s Kinexys business has continued developing infrastructure for payments and tokenized financial transactions. In its October announcement, the bank said the platform had processed more than $4 trillion in cumulative transactions and was averaging approximately $7 billion a day. Those figures concern Kinexys’s operations as a whole and should not be presented as Ethereum mainnet JPM Coin volume. The bank has not disclosed the portion attributable to JPMD transactions on the newly supported network. Beyond Ethereum and Base, JPMorgan has been working with Digital Asset to bring JPM Coin to the Canton Network, which focuses on institutional financial transactions and privacy. On January 7, 2026, Digital Asset and Kinexys announced plans to issue JPMD natively on Canton. The proposal covers the issuance, transfer and redemption of the deposit token within a blockchain environment designed for regulated financial institutions. The planned Canton integration followed the November Base launch, giving the bank a separate path for supporting institutions that require additional transaction privacy. Canton’s architecture allows financial participants to coordinate transactions while restricting the visibility of sensitive information. Digital Asset has positioned the network for use cases involving institutional securities, payments and collateral management. The January agreement described a phased integration through 2026, beginning with the technical and business infrastructure needed for native JPMD issuance and redemption. Digital Asset and JPMorgan said the collaboration could later consider additional Kinexys products, including Blockchain Deposit Accounts. The announcement did not confirm that every proposed service had already entered production. Naveen Mallela, global co-head of Kinexys, said at the time that the planned Canton integration would combine bank-issued deposits with near-real-time blockchain settlement. The companies did not provide a specific date for a completed public launch. The October Ethereum expansion has been announced separately from that Canton development. The bank’s January release remains a statement of intent concerning phased Canton deployment, and no completed Canton mainnet launch was established by the materials reviewed. title: JPMorgan Expands JPM Coin to Ethereum for Institutional Payments - TradingView
content: JPMorgan’s decision to bring JPM Coin (JPMD) to Ethereum adds another network to the bank’s blockchain operations, raising a broader question about how financial institutions will manage digital money across different blockchains. The US dollar deposit token launched on Base in November 2025. Its Ethereum expansion gives eligible institutional clients another network for transferring bank deposits, while JPMorgan continues developing blockchain-based financial products across its business. The move is not a shift away from Base. Instead, it extends JPM Coin’s reach to Ethereum, where JPMorgan already has tokenized money market funds, including MONY and JLTXX. JPMorgan’s Blockchain Operations Are Spreading Across Networks This move highlights how banks are exploring multiple blockchain networks rather than relying on a single platform for every financial product. Base provided the initial public blockchain network for JPM Coin. Ethereum now adds access to a separate ecosystem of tokenized assets and financial applications. JPMorgan has also explored native JPM Coin issuance on Canton, according to previously announced plans reported by PrimeXBT. This approach allows the bank to develop its blockchain services around different institutional requirements. However, operating across multiple networks does not automatically mean assets or deposits can move freely between them. Each deployment depends on its own technical setup, access rules and integration arrangements. Tokenized Funds and Bank Deposits Serve Different Roles JPMorgan’s Ethereum presence includes both investment products and its newly expanded deposit token, but the two serve different purposes. MONY and JLTXX represent interests in tokenized money market funds. JPM Coin, by contrast, represents US dollar deposits held at JPMorgan and is intended for payments and institutional transactions. Having these products on the same network creates potential for closer integration. However, JPMorgan has not confirmed that all subscriptions, redemptions or settlements for its tokenized funds will use JPM Coin. The distinction matters because issuing financial products on a blockchain is only one part of building a complete digital financial system. Institutions must also establish how money moves, how transactions are settled and which participants can access the services. JPMorgan’s Ethereum deployment establishes another option for institutional clients, but the wider impact will depend on actual usage. Key indicators include the volume of transactions conducted through JPM Coin on Ethereum, the number of participating institutions and whether the network supports new integrations with tokenized financial products. Until those figures become available, the expansion is best understood as an extension of JPMorgan’s blockchain infrastructure rather than evidence that institutional finance has moved away from traditional banking systems. JPMorgan remains the issuer of the deposit token, and access is restricted to eligible institutional clients. Ethereum provides another network for its use, while the bank continues to control the banking relationship and participation requirements. Select market data provided by ICE Data Services. title: Robot factories and hypersonic missiles: JPMorgan Chase's first $5 billion of defense investments - CNBC
content:
JPMorgan Chase has made $5 billion in startup investments in the first year of its U.S. security and resiliency initiative, the company said Monday, a faster-than-expected pace that indicates the bank is finding plentiful opportunities in emerging defense, manufacturing and supply chain firms. The bank, which last year said it would deploy $10 billion into startups over a decade, may expand the program beyond that initial dollar amount, JPMorgan co-President Doug Petno told CNBC in an interview. Todd Combs, the former Berkshire Hathaway executive who leads the JPMorgan group in charge of making startup investments, has “hit the ground running,” Petno said. “He’s done a great job and put us in some really interesting companies,” he added. Most of those investments have yet to be disclosed, but two known stakes seem emblematic of the project’s mission to bolster companies that are needed for a more dangerous and chaotic era of geopolitics. JPMorgan, the biggest U.S. bank by assets, has taken direct stakes in defense-related startups Hadrian and Castelion. Wars in Ukraine and the Middle East, as well as trade disputes with China, have threatened the flow of energy and key components needed for U.S. industries and defense, which spurred JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon into creating the initiative a year ago. He put Petno, widely seen as one of two key possible successors, in charge of the overall investment project. Combs, a former board member of the bank, reports directly to Dimon. The scope of the project extends beyond supply chain, defense and manufacturing to include frontier technologies and the pharmaceutical and health-tech industries. “There’s a lot of really interesting companies that have been working to solve some of these problems,” Petno said. These “early venture-stage, advanced manufacturing companies have found ways to build these capabilities in the U.S.” rather than relying on overseas trading partners, he said. In August, the bank helped lead a $1.4 billion funding round for Hadrian, which builds automated factories that make parts for the defense, aerospace and maritime sectors. A California factory run by Hadrian has 10 robots for every human employee, according to the startup’s founder. That month, JPMorgan was also involved in a $1 billion funding round for Castelion, whose flagship product is a relatively low-cost hypersonic missile called Blackbeard. Castelion was founded in late 2022 by a group of former SpaceX engineers. “Our approach is to find generational companies and partner with them for the long term,” Combs said in a statement Monday. “Putting more than $5 billion to work in our first year shows how many exceptional businesses are building in industries that strengthen critical supply chains,” Combs said. JPMorgan making billions of dollars of direct investments in nascent companies is a departure from its usual role as a lender and advisor. Before the defense initiative, the bank had moved away from taking startup stakes, which can be relatively risky bets on unproven technologies. JPMorgan spun off its private equity business, One Equity Partners, more than a decade ago. In its more traditional role, JPMorgan has also financed and facilitated more than $230 billion for industries that support American national interests, according to the bank. That part of its security and resiliency project, meant to hit $1.5 trillion over 10 years, is led by Jay Horine, a former co-head of investment banking. JPMorgan built a team for the project of about three dozen bankers, who are aided by hundreds more across the firm, as it expanded the initiative to Europe and Canada. Its bankers are mapping distribution lines for key products, from submarines and missiles to aircraft, to identify suppliers that may lack the capital or capacity to meet rising demand, according to Petno. JPMorgan is also in regular communication with the U.S. Department of Defense and Department of Commerce about the government’s needs, he said. Got a confidential news tip? We want to hear from you. title: JPMorgan Launches JPM Coin on Ethereum Network - ForkLog
content: JPMorgan Chase, the largest American bank, has launched its deposit token, JPM Coin (JPMD), on the Ethereum mainnet. This was reported by Bloomberg, citing a statement from the organization. According to Emma Landrio, head of the bank’s blockchain division Kinexys Labs, crypto companies can use the asset for on-chain payments, while financial institutions can use it for transaction settlements and as collateral. JPMorgan chose Ethereum due to its liquidity and because the network is already used by its clients, she explained. Unlike regular stablecoins, JPMD is a commercial bank obligation to the depositor. The token is not intended for free circulation among retail users. Transactions with the asset are available only to approved institutional clients of JPMorgan. Transfers are possible only between whitelisted addresses. JPMorgan launched JPM Coin on a public network in November 2025. At that time, the token became available to institutional clients on Base, an L2 solution for Ethereum by Coinbase. Prior to this, pilot operations were conducted by Mastercard, Coinbase, and B2C2. Participants tested the issuance and redemption of JPMD with near-instant settlements. The then-head of the blockchain division, Naveen Mallela, described deposit tokens as an alternative to “stablecoins” for institutional clients. He stated that such instruments could potentially generate income in the future. In January 2026, Kinexys and Digital Asset announced plans to launch JPM Coin on the Canton Network, a blockchain aimed at financial institutions. The bank intends to issue the token across multiple networks and eventually add support for other currencies. Earlier, in December 2025, JPMorgan introduced its first tokenized money market fund, My OnChain Net Yield Fund (MONY), based on Ethereum. The product is aimed at qualified investors and allows them to earn income from dollar instruments via blockchain.
